## VIC options and activation: `implicit-scheme` 1 or 9, one block in $x_1$ (`ImplicitOptions`) {#sec-ch07-vic-options}

### Summary

The scheme value is a bit field. Bit 0 makes $x_1$ implicit and bit 3 selects the full system; bits 1 and 2 only
change the time-step bound of @sec-ch07-cfl. Only the values 0, 1 and 9 build. Any other value stops the run when
the solver object is constructed. A VIC run also needs the whole $x_1$ column on one rank and a constant
gravity.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Reads `integration/implicit-scheme` and decides whether a run has a vertically implicit correction
(VIC), and whether it solves the 3 x 3 or the 5 x 5 column system; @eq-ch07-vic-size.

**Data.** In: `integration/implicit-scheme` [integer], `implicit-advection-cfl` and `shear-cfl` [-], and the
$x_1$ block count `nb1` [count] from the YAML card, read once per block at construction. Out: the scheme type
(`none`, `vic-partial`, `vic-full`) and the system size $N = 3$ or $5$. Units and mass basis: none, no physical
quantity enters. Check cases: every value 0 to 9, the cfl key defaults and refusals, `nb1` 1 and 2.

**Placement.** At setup.

**Activation.** `integration/implicit-scheme`: 0 or absent (explicit), 1 (`vic-partial`), 9 (`vic-full`);
`implicit-advection-cfl` (default 1) and `shear-cfl` (default 0), see @sec-ch07-cfl.

**Guarantee / limits.** Any other value is refused.

**Evidence.** Tests: `type()` is `none`, `vic-partial`, `vic-full` for 0, 1, 9 and 5 raises,
{{< code tests/test_implicit_options_type.py main >}} (exact); 1 gives size 3 and 9 size 5,
{{< code tests/test_backward_substitution.cpp implicit_options.parses_implicit_scheme_bits >}} (exact); 3 is refused
at construction, {{< code tests/test_hydro_options.cpp hydro_options.reject_unsupported_implicit_scheme >}} (exact);
not run at the pin. Check: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_options_check.py`, output `vic_options_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C4]`; the committed output prints PASS and the measured value of each claim, not the threshold it is held to, so the thresholds are **missing evidence** in the output; the check ports the code at the pin.
:::

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive. With $s$ the scheme value, the block size of the column system is

$$
N(s) = 3 + 2\,\big(\lfloor s/8 \rfloor \bmod 2\big) ,
$$ {#eq-ch07-vic-size}

so `vic-partial` solves for $(\rho, \rho v_1, E)$ and `vic-full` for $(\rho, \rho v_1, \rho v_2, \rho v_3, E)$, with $v_1$ the
$x_1$ velocity [check `src/snapy_report/ch07/vic_options_check.py`, output `vic_options_check.out`, `[C1]`]. Here
$\rho$ is the total density: the species ride on it and are redistributed afterwards (@sec-ch07-vic-redistribute).

In the code, @eq-ch07-vic-size is `size` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.hpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::size >}}).

### Numerical method

See @fig-ch07-vic-options for the bits.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch07-vic-options
#| fig-cap: "The value of integration/implicit-scheme as four bits. Bit 0 makes $x_1$ implicit; bit 3 selects the full $5\\times5$ system. The values that build are 0 (explicit: no solver object), 1 (vic-partial) and 9 (vic-full); any other value stops with Unsupported implicit scheme (vermillion). Bits 1 and 2 only change the time-step bound."
#| fig-alt: "Three rows of four bit boxes for the values 0, 1 and 9, with the set bits filled green, and a red note that other values are refused."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch07.fig_vic_options import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The options come from the `integration` block, which pyharp's integrator also reads, so its keys are checked
against both readers ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=1 >}}). A value of 0 returns no options at all from `from_yaml`, so 0 is
a true explicit spelling that also runs with several blocks in $x_1$ ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}).
The two bound keys without a scheme are an error, not ignored (`[C3]`). `implicit-advection-cfl` must be finite and
positive, and `shear-cfl` finite and non-negative (`[C2]`).

`HydroImpl` creates the solver object, `picorr`, only when the options exist ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}). Its `reset`
calls `type`, which is what refuses an unsupported value ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::reset >}}). The
first correction then checks with `is_physical_boundary` that both $x_1$ faces of the block are physical
boundaries, since the column solve has no cross-rank coupling ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}). It also requires a constant gravity, through
`grav` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}) (`[C4]`).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The VIC is $x_1$ only. A run cut into several blocks in $x_1$ cannot use it.
:::

1. **Bits that do not build.** Bits 1 and 2 are read by the time-step bound, but no value that sets them builds,
   so a $x_2$ or $x_3$ implicit direction cannot be reached.
2. **Late nb1 check.** The one-block condition is checked at the first correction, not when the options are read.
